bull.b: The owned 26 MW platform and low blended electricity cost provide a durable operating foundation for bitcoin mining and future AI/HPC hosting. Control of energized capacity may support competitive costs and expansion if the company secures customers and capital.

Higher bitcoin output and year-over-year revenue growth indicate improving scale and utilization of the mining platform. This supports the existing revenue base, although sustained benefits still depend on network conditions, operating efficiency and asset economics.

The AI/HPC initiative is progressing from concept toward an operational platform, with marketplace validation, additional hardware and certification work. These steps could broaden revenue beyond bitcoin mining and improve asset utilization over the medium term.

bear.b: Large recurring losses relative to revenue show that the current business model is not yet economically sustainable. Continued unprofitability can erode equity, limit reinvestment capacity and increase dependence on external financing to fund operations.

Persistent cash outflows and a very small cash balance create structural funding pressure. The company may need repeated financing or asset monetization, leaving less flexibility to absorb operating setbacks or invest in its planned infrastructure expansion.

bear.t: Heavy bitcoin collateralization and short-tenor debt
bear.b: Pledging most bitcoin holdings and relying on financing that requires renewal every 30 days exposes the company to refinancing, collateral and liquidity risk. A weaker operating environment or inability to renew could constrain assets and disrupt strategic execution.
